findings.F1: Across all trends, a 20-day fall of 10 to 25 % is followed by a 5-day excess return of -2.57 % (t -3.72, 281 non-overlapping cases), while falls deeper than 25 % are followed by none (-0.03 %, t -0.03, 186 cases). Weighting falls of 0 to 25 % by their depth, continuation shows with t 2.06 over 178 independent days, and it points the same way in 2018 (t 1.80), 2019 (t 1.60) and 2020 (t 0.75) but not in 2021 (t -0.05).
findings.F2: The continuation after a 20-day fall is largest outside falling markets and is graded by depth there. In a rising market, a 20-day return of 0 to -10 % is followed by +1.02 %, -10 to -25 % by -6.02 %, and below -25 % by -9.96 %. In a choppy market the same bands give -2.55 %, -7.32 % and -11.23 %. In a falling market they give only -2.45 %, -1.79 % and +0.54 %.
findings.F3: The tested volume effect shows in the bars where the idea acts, but it is small. In falling markets, the lowest third of the 30-day volume change is followed by -2.17 % (t -2.20, 134 cases) and the highest third by +0.94 % (t 0.89). The correlation of volume change with the 5-day excess return is +0.13 for 20-day falls of 10 to 25 % (t 1.75, 179 cases) and +0.13 for falls beyond 25 % (t 1.37, 114 cases).
findings.F4: In rising markets the volume relation reverses sign. Volume change and the 5-day excess return correlate at -0.25 when the 20-day rise exceeds 15 % (t -3.10, 150 cases) and at -0.23 in rising calm bars (t -2.91, 159 cases). Taken by day, the rising-calm dry-up-long reading is only t 1.57 (63 days), and it reverses in 2020 (t -2.18): it does not stand out once the cases of a day are taken together.
findings.F5: The book earns the same from both sides, +0.232 % per bar short (1,203 bars) and +0.233 % per bar long (921 bars). Its gain sits in a few windows: w7 (+1.82), w13 (+1.51), w16 (+1.24) and w15 (+0.67) carry it, while w9 (-0.28) and w14 (-0.08) lose. This concentration is what holds Calmar at 0.41, since cost is not the problem: the unusual move is 9.8 times the cost of a trade.
findings.F6: The short trades are carried by a few large wins: their mean net return is +2.20 % against a median of -0.70 % (445 trades). The long trades have a mean of +3.19 % and a median of +2.63 % (316 trades).
findings.F7: A weekday pattern (Monday +1.70 %, t 2.42; Thursday -1.85 %, t -2.50, about 240 cases each, over 7 groups) does not stand out against the number of groups looked at. Neither does the choppy-agitated volume correlation (r 0.34, t 2.47, 49 cases, carried by ZEC).

ideas.idea: In a rising market, the deeper the coin's fall over the last 20 days, the further it keeps falling over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader in a rising market does not buy a 20-day pullback as a dip; he leans short on it, and harder the deeper it goes.
ideas.name: rising market pullback continues
